metric: Native engine steady-state completion tokens per second; pretokenized, no HTTP.
aggregation: Median of three process warm medians; each process has one first pass and three warm passes. Backends/concurrencies interleaved.

timing.native_core_field: core_wall_s (sum of synchronized wave intervals); legacy wall_s and inherited notes are not used for core throughput.
timing.initialization_note: Engine init only, not full process startup; vLLM includes model compilation/graph capture. Existing disk caches retained; not clean-machine cold start.
timing.preprocess_note: Native preprocess includes input read/parse; vLLM preprocess is formatting/tokenization only. Excluded from core and not a direct speed comparison.

configuration.native: NVFP4 fused GGUF, F16 KV, fixed waves, batch/ubatch 2048, GPU prefix sampling, one CPU sampling thread
configuration.vllm: NVFP4 linear weights, CUTLASS W4A4, BF16 shared embedding/head and KV, continuous batching, token budget 2048, KV budget 3/6 GiB

historical_binary_control.metric: Original full hy-batch wall, includes tokenization/output I/O/first graph preparation; model init excluded.
historical_binary_control.finding: The prior approximately 20 percent old-to-current regression was not reproduced using exact historical/current EXEs with identical inference DLLs. Historic 5426.65 versus present values remains unexplained without historic clock/load telemetry.

limitations: Quantization/calibration and embedding precision differ; this compares the two complete engine configurations, not identical weights or GPU kernels.
Native fixed waves and vLLM continuous batching retain each backend scheduling behavior.
GPU clocks not locked; telemetry uses 100 ms receive timestamps and phase bounds. Native telemetry windows include small output gaps excluded from core wall.
No isolated prefill/decode GPU timing: llama_perf batched decode is classified as p_eval and cannot provide that split.
CUTLASS quality result remains chrF++ 52.0639 versus native 52.5523 on the separate holdout; not lossless.
Short fixed workload on one GPU; not a universal gain or optimality proof.
related_evidence: vllm-windows-migration.json retains quality, HTTP and earlier tuning experiments; it is supplemental to this matched core comparison.
